rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ calls the referenced wording undesirable.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الفتح: هي مرغوب عنها

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Thābit reads يهلك with ḍamma on the initial yāʾ and kasra on the lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن ثابت: يهلك، بضم الياء وكسر اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses القوم الفاسقون in the accusative and says the verse warns and threatens.
rows.anchor: إلا القوم الفاسقون: بالنصب، وفي هذه الآية وعيد وإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basqat al-nakhla means that the palm grew tall; he cites a poem describing lofty palms whose fruit pickers cannot reach.
rows.anchor: بسقت النخلة بسوقا: طالت، قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb بسق can mean to rise above one's companions; the verse by Ibn Nufayl applies it to a man surpassing Fazāra.
rows.anchor: وبسق فلان على أصحابه: أي علاهم، ومنه قول ابن نوفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بسقت can also mean that a ewe gave birth, while أَبْسَقَت describes a she-camel whose colostrum appears before delivery.
rows.anchor: ويقال: بسقت الشاة: ولدت، وأبسقت الناقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حَادَ عن الشيء means to turn away or incline from it; he gives the verbal nouns حيودا، حيدة، and حيدودة.
rows.anchor: حاد عن الشيء: مال عنه، حيودا وحيدة وحيدودة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ identifies the two jugulars with the span between the throat and the two collarbones.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: هو ما بين الحلقوم والعلباوين

rows.speaker: الأثرم
rows.claim: Al-Athram calls the jugular the body's river and lists the names of major veins in different body parts.
rows.anchor: وقال الأثرم: هو نهر الجسد، هو في القلب: الوتين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī describes the jugulars as two veins flanking the front of the neck and connecting to the aorta; he explains the name by the spirit's passage.
rows.anchor: والوريدان عرقان مكتنفان بصحفتي العنق في مقدمها متصلان بالوتين

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the exegetes unanimously regard Sūrat Qāf as Meccan.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: بإجماع من المتأولين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda say the surah is Meccan except for the verse about creating the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وقتادة: مكية إلا آية، وهي قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah follows the previous one by exposing false profession of faith, denial of the Messenger, and denial of resurrection, which leads into the disbelievers' wonder.
rows.anchor: ومناسبتها لآخر ما قبلها، أنه تعالى أخبر أن أولئك الذين قالوا آمنا، لم يكن إيمانهم حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter Qāf has eleven conflicting interpretations without evidence for any; Abū Ḥayyān omits their enumeration.
rows.anchor: اختلف المفسرون في مدلوله على أحد عشر قولا متعارضة، لا دليل على صحة شيء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is sworn by and al-majīd describes its nobility above other scriptures; the oath's answer is omitted and inferred from what follows.
rows.anchor: والقرآن مقسم به والمجيد صفته، وهو الشريف على غيره من الكتب، والجواب محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supplies the omitted oath answer as: the Prophet came warning them of resurrection, but they did not accept him.
rows.anchor: وتقديره: أنك جئتهم منذرا بالبعث، فلم يقبلوا

rows.speaker: الأخفش والمبرد والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash, al-Mubarrad, and al-Zajjāj take the oath's answer to mean that they will surely be resurrected.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش، والمبرد، والزجاج: تقديره لتبعثن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed oath answers are 'We know what the earth diminishes,' 'No word is uttered,' 'They wondered,' or 'In that is a reminder'; Abū Ḥayyān calls these weak, though al-Tirmidhī preferred the last.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الجواب مذكور، فعن الأخفش قد علمنا ما تنقص الأرض منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pause Qāf; ʿĪsā opens it, al-Ḥasan and others give it kasra, and Hārūn and Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ give it ḍamma; he explains the vowels grammatically.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: قاف بسكون الفاء، ويفتحها عيسى، ويكسرها الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'they wondered' most naturally refers to the disbelievers, whose ingrained disbelief explains their reaction; an alternative makes it refer to all people by nature.
rows.anchor: فقال الكافرون تنبيها على القلة الموجبة للعجب، وهو أنهم قد جبلوا على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'this is a strange thing' may point to a human messenger or to the resurrection announced; al-Zamakhsharī takes it as the return, which Abū Ḥayyān finds far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى ما تضمنه الإنذار، وهو الإخبار بالبعث

rows.speaker: الأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر وابن وثاب والأعمش وابن عتبة
rows.claim: These readers pronounce إذا with one hamza as a declarative form; it may conceal an interrogative hamza or state their claim that they will return after becoming dust.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج، وشيبة، وأبو جعفر، وابن وثاب، والأعمش، وابن عتبة عن ابن عامر: إذا بهمزة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the interrogative reading, the time expression depends on an omitted verb meaning 'Will we be raised when we die?'; 'that' points to resurrection, which they deem remote.
rows.anchor: فالظرف منصوب بمضمر، أي: أنبعث إذا متنا؟ وإليه الإشارة بقوله ذلك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows رجع to mean 'the returned thing' and to be God's own expression of their rejection; Abū Ḥayyān calls this interpretation astonishing and unintelligible to Arabs.
rows.anchor: وكون ذلك رجع بعيد بمعنى مرجوع، وأنه من كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and most exegetes say the earth diminishes the dead's flesh, bones, and traces; God's knowledge of this refutes doubts about restoring them.
rows.anchor: أي من لحومهم وعظامهم وآثارهم، قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī reads the phrase as what is buried in the earth from the dead, implying a threat.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: أي ما يحصل في بطن الأرض من موتاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preserved book either retains and gathers everything without loss, is protected from decay, or denotes God's knowledge and enumeration.
rows.anchor: أي حافظ لما فيه جامع، لا يفوت منه شيء، أو محفوظ من البلى والتغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound report says the earth consumes the son of Adam except the tailbone, a tiny bone from which he is reassembled.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر الثابت أن الأرض تأكل ابن آدم إلا عجب الذنب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the second بل as advancing from wonder to the graver offense of denying the truth of prophethood confirmed by miracles.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أنهم جاءوا بما هو أفظع من تعجبهم، وهو التكذيب بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputed referent of al-ḥaqq is the Quran, resurrection, the Messenger, or Islam.
rows.anchor: والحق: القرآن، أو البعث، أو الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، أو الإسلام، أقوال

rows.speaker: الجحدري
rows.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads لما with a kasra on the lām and a light mīm, making ما a verbal noun and the lām a preposition meaning 'when they received it.'
rows.anchor: والجحدري: لما جاءهم، بكسر اللام وتخفيف الميم، وما مصدرية

rows.speaker: الضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Zayd explain مريج as confused; Qatāda says varied, al-Ḥasan entangled, and Abū Hurayra corrupt.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك، وابن زيد: مختلط: مرة ساحر، ومرة شاعر، ومرة كاهن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses مريج as a reprehensible or confused affair; Abū Ḥayyān says its basic sense is instability and agitation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المريج: الأمر المنكر، وعنه أيضا مختلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word مريج evokes instability, as a ring that slips on a finger because its wearer has grown thin; he cites poetry with the same word.
rows.anchor: والأصل فيه الاضطراب والقلق. مرج الخاتم في إصبعي، إذا قلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their confusion is reflected in a succession of reactions: rejecting the warning, wondering, doubting resurrection, and then denying the message.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الأمر المريج، باعتبار انتقال أفكارهم فيما جاء به المنذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After denying resurrection and the Messenger, people should look at God's signs: the elevated, ornamented heavens are free from gaps or flaws.
rows.anchor: أفلم ينظروا حين كفروا بالبعث وبما جاء به الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spread the earth, set firm mountains to keep it from tilting, and grew beautiful kinds of plants that delight the eye.
rows.anchor: والأرض مددناها: بسطناها، وألقينا فيها رواسي، أي جبالا ثوابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers put تبصرة and ذكرى in the accusative as objects of implied verbs; Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads تبصرة in the nominative, coordinated with ذكر, describing creation as a lesson.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تبصرة وذكرى بالنصب، وهما منصوبان بفعل مضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ināba is one who returns to his Lord and reflects on the wonders of God's making.
rows.anchor: لكل عبد منيب: أي راجع إلى ربه مفكر في بدائع صنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessed rain means abundant in benefit; الحصيد is a shortened expression for the grain-bearing crop that is harvested.
rows.anchor: ماء مباركا: أي كثير المنفعة، وحب الحصيد: أي الحب الحصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: باسقات means tall palms and is a circumstantial description expressing a state they will reach as they grow; النخل is a collective noun used in masculine, feminine, or plural forms.
rows.anchor: باسقات: أي طوالا في العلو، وهو منصوب على الحال، وهي حال مقدرة

rows.speaker: قطبة بن مالك
rows.claim: Qutba ibn Mālik transmits that the Prophet read باصقات with ṣād; Abū Ḥayyān calls it a dialect of Banū al-ʿAnbar that substitutes ṣād for sīn in specified contexts.
rows.anchor: وروى قطبة بن مالك، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، أنه قرأ: باصقات بالصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نضيد means arranged in layers; early dates remain packed together inside the spathe, then separate when they emerge.
rows.anchor: نضيد: أي منضود بعضه فوق بعض، يريد كثرة الطلع وتراكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رزقا is either a cognate accusative because 'we grew' means 'we provided,' or a purpose object.
rows.anchor: ورزقا نصب على المصدر، لأن معنى: وأنبتنا رزقنا، أو على أنه مفعول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers lighten ميتا, while Abū Jaʿfar and Khālid double the yāʾ; the resurrection of people is likened to reviving a dead land.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ميتا بالتخفيف وأبو جعفر، وخالد: بالتثقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He pairs three heavenly signs with three earthly ones: building with spreading, celestial adornment with rooted mountains, and growth with the heavens' freedom from fissures.
rows.anchor: وذكر تعالى في السماء ثلاثة: البناء والتزين ونفي الفروج، وفي الأرض ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vegetation examples distinguish yearly picked produce whose plant remains, crops sown for one or two years, and mixed kinds; crops are mostly food while fruits are largely treats and sometimes food.
rows.anchor: ونبه فيما تعلق به الإنبات على ما يقطف كل سنة ويبقى أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first creation is the gradual formation of a human from a drop; the verse challenges those who deny that the second creation is possible.
rows.anchor: أفعيينا بالخلق الأول: وهو إنشاء الإنسان من نطفة على التدريج

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla and several transmitters read عيينا with a doubled yāʾ; Abū Ḥayyān derives it from dialectal assimilation without separating the doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة، والوليد بن مسلم، والقورصي عن أبي جعفر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the first creation with Adam and paraphrases the challenge: did We fail to create him, then somehow fail to create people again?
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: الخلق الأول آدم عليه السلام، والمعنى: أعجزنا عن الخلق الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage rebukes disbelievers and establishes a clear proof against their denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وهذا توقيف للكفار، وتوبيخ وإقامة الحجة الواضحة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لبس means confusion, doubt, or bewilderment, illustrated by ʿAlī's remark to someone mistaken about the truth.
rows.anchor: بل هم في لبس: أي خلط وشبهة وحيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new creation means resurrection from the graves.
rows.anchor: من خلق جديد: أي من البعث من القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الإنسان may denote the human species generally or Adam specifically.
rows.anchor: والإنسان اسم جنس. وقيل: آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's nearness is nearness in knowledge of the person and his states, not spatial presence; حبل الوريد is an image for extreme closeness.
rows.anchor: قرب علم به وبأحواله، لا يخفى عليه شيء من خفياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥabl al-warīd is a vein named by comparison to a cord; the phrase is explanatory, or may mean the cord at the shoulder, which shares the neck region with the jugular.
rows.anchor: والحبل: العرق الذي شبه بواحد الحبال، وإضافته إلى الوريد للبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase إذ يتلقى can depend on 'nearer,' or introduce a command to recall the recorded deeds, death's agony, the trumpet, and each soul's guide and witness.
rows.anchor: والعامل في إذ أقرب. وقيل: اذكر، قيل: ويحسن تقدير اذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two receivers are angels recording good and bad deeds; al-Ḥasan instead says each person has four guardians, two by day and two by night.
rows.anchor: والمتلقيان: الملكان الموكلان بكل إنسان ملك اليمين يكتب الحسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قعيد may function as a collective or intensive singular, stand for two angels, be omitted after the first mention, or be delayed from its expected place; al-Farrāʾ says it itself covers dual and plural.
rows.anchor: وقعيدة: مفرد، فاحتمل أن يكون معناه: مقاعد

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو الحواراء
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Abū al-Ḥawwarāʾ say every utterance is recorded, even a sick person's groan.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وأبو الحواراء: يكتب عليه كل شيء حتى أنينه في مرضه

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say both angels record all speech, but God retains good and bad deeds and erases the rest; ʿIkrima limits recording to good and evil speech.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن، وقتادة: يكتبان جميع الكلام، فيثبت الله تعالى من ذلك الحسنات والسيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The location where the two angels sit is disputed, and Abū Ḥayyān says no report about it is sound; رقيب means watching and عتيد means present.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في تعيين قعود الملكين، ولا يصح فيه شيء. رقيب: ملك يرقب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the record is folded when a person dies; another report says the person will be told to read his book on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: فإذا مات، طويت صحيفته. وقيل: له يوم القيامة اقرأ كتابك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The death-agony is what overtakes a person at death; the bāʾ in بالحق may mark its arrival with the truth of the person's felicity or misery, or its being bound to truth.
rows.anchor: وسكرة الموت: ما يعتري الإنسان عند نزاعه، والباء في بالحق للتعدية

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads سكران as a plural form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: سكران جمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تحيد means to turn away; a person avoids thinking about approaching death and hopes it lies far off, though the wording directly addresses the dying person.
rows.anchor: أي تميل. تقول: أعيش كذا وأعيش كذا، فمتى فكر في قرب الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day of warning refers to the day the trumpet is blown; it is called by the threat though it also contains God's promise, to instill fear.
rows.anchor: وأضاف اليوم إلى الوعيد، وإن كان يوم الوعد والوعيد معا على سبيل التخويف

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان ومجاهد
rows.claim: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, Mujāhid, and others identify the guide and witness as two angels assigned to each person.
rows.anchor: قال عثمان بن عفان، ومجاهد وغيره: ملكان موكلان بكل إنسان

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra says the guide is an angel and the witness is the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة: السائق ملك، والشهيد النبي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say an angel drives the person and the person's own limbs testify; Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that this cannot cover righteous and wicked people alike.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والضحاك: السائق ملك، والشهيد: جوارح الإنسان

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim identifies the guide as Satan, a view Abū Ḥayyān calls weak.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: السائق شيطان، وهو قول ضعيف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the guide and witness as two angels, or as one angel doing both; Abū Ḥayyān rejects his grammatical argument that كل نفس becomes definite through annexation.
rows.anchor: هذا كلام ساقط لا يصدر عن مبتدىء في النحو

rows.speaker: الجحدري
rows.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads the pronouns in كنت and غطاءك with feminine agreement, following the meaning of نفس.
rows.anchor: والجحدري: بكسرها على مخاطبة النفس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وصالح بن كيسان والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the rebuke addresses a heedless disbeliever at the resurrection: his negligence concerned the consequence of disbelief.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وصالح بن كيسان، والضحاك: يقال للكافر الغافل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The veil is a metaphor for heedlessness covering the person or his eyes; once heedlessness is removed, the truth that he ignored becomes visible.
rows.anchor: وكنى بالغطاء عن الغفلة، كأنها غطت جميعه أو عينيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the sharpened sight as literal eyesight focused on the person's balance and other terrors of resurrection, while the preceding view takes it as insight.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو بصر العين، أي احتد التفاته إلى ميزانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first companion who says 'this is ready' is a keeper of Hell presenting the punishment prepared for the disbeliever; عتيد means present.
rows.anchor: وقال قرينه: أي من زبانية جهنم، هذا: العذاب الذي لدي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies this companion as the angel assigned to drive the person, who announces that the disbeliever he brings is ready.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: قرينه: الملك الموكل بسوقه

rows.speaker: الزهراوي
rows.claim: Al-Zahrawī transmits the view that the companion here is the person's devil; Abū Ḥayyān calls that weak, while distinguishing the devil in the later dispute.
rows.anchor: وقيل قرينه: شيطانه، وهذا ضعيف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī identifies the companion as the devil appointed to the person, who claims to have prepared him for Hell by misleading him; Abū Ḥayyān attributes this view to Mujāhid.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to cast into Hell addresses the two angels who drive and witness; other readings take it as two tormenting angels or as a command to one companion, but he prefers the apparent dual wording.
rows.anchor: الخطاب من الله للملكين: السائق والشهيد

rows.speaker: المجاهد وجماعة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and others say the command is addressed to one person, either the guide or a keeper of Hell; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the strained alternatives to the dual reading.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وجماعة: هو قول إما للسائق، وإما للذي هو من الزبانية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan has the command read with a light emphatic nūn, a noncanonical reading that conflicts with the transmitted tawātur form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: ألقين بنون التوكيد الخفيفة، وهي شاذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further gloss takes مريب to mean someone suspected or accused.
rows.anchor: وقيل: متهم الذي جوزوا فيه

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: Qatāda, Mujāhid, and ʿIkrima specify zakāt as the good the miser withholds; others say the phrase means stinginess or preventing a nephew from embracing faith.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة ومجاهد وعكرمة: يعني الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers a general meaning for withholding good, covering wealth and other forms of good.
rows.anchor: والأحسن عموم الخير في المال وغيره

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains مريب as doubting God or resurrection; another gloss is a person held suspect.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: شاك في الله أو في البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya's suggestion that the definite الذي describes كفار as grammatically invalid: a definite adjective cannot describe a noun introduced as indefinite.
rows.anchor: وهذا ليس بشيء لو وصفت النكرة بأوصاف كثيرة لم يجز أن توصف بالمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The missing conjunction before 'his companion said' marks a newly opened exchange: the disbeliever blames his companion, who denies causing his rebellion, though the devil in fact misled him by whispering and embellishment.
rows.anchor: وكذب القرين، قد أطغاه بوسوسته وتزيينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's prohibition on disputing is a new reply in the scene; the dispute is in the abode of recompense and at the reckoning, and the prior warning left no excuse.
rows.anchor: لا تختصموا لدي أي في دار الجزاء وموقف الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's decree cannot be changed once enacted; al-Farrāʾ instead glosses it as God not being deceived because He knows all things.
rows.anchor: ما أمضيته لا يمكن تبديله. وقال الفراء: ما يكذب لدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about having sent the warning beforehand may mean God's word preceded them, or that He delivered the warning; the delivery occurred in worldly life.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون بمعنى تقدمت، أي قد تقدم قولي لكم ملتبسا بالوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links "I am not unjust to the servants" to a similar explanation at the end of Āl ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: تقدم شرح مثله في أواخر آل عمران

rows.speaker: الأعرج وشيبة ونافع وأبو بكر والحسن وأبو رجاء وأبو جعفر والأعمش
rows.claim: These readers recite the verb of saying with third-person yāʾ; others use first-person nūn, and ʿAbd Allāh, al-Ḥasan, and al-Aʿmash also transmit a passive form.
rows.anchor: قرأ يوم يقول، بياء الغيبة الأعرج، وشيبة، ونافع، وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows يوم to depend on the trumpet-blowing clause, but Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because many intervening sentences separate the verb and its complement.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد جدا، قد فصل على هذا القول بين العامل والمعمول بجمل كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question 'Are you full?' is a rhetorical confirmation, since God knows Hell's state; it may be literal dialogue, directed to Hell's keepers, or a vivid personification.
rows.anchor: وهل امتلأت: تقرير وتوقيف، لا سؤال استفهام حقيقة

rows.speaker: الحسن وعمرو وواصل
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, ʿAmr, and Wāṣil say Hell was already full and cannot increase, comparing the expression to asking whether ʿAqīl left a house when none remained.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن، وعمرو، وواصل: كانت ملأى وقت السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Not far away' means the garden was brought near in place; the wording reinforces the promised nearness.
rows.anchor: غير بعيد: مكانا غير بعيد، وهو تأكيد لأزلفت

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read the promise clause in the third person, referring to what was promised, while most readers address the believers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ما توعدون خطاب للمؤمنين وابن كثير، وأبو عمرو: بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes 'one who feared the Merciful unseen' a second dependent apposition under 'for every returning and watchful person'; Abū Ḥayyān disputes his claim that relative clauses take only الذي forms.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله: ولا يوصف من بين الموصولات إلا بالذي، فالحصر ليس بصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'who feared the Merciful unseen' can mean fearing God's punishment though He is unseen, fearing in private, or fearing because of the unseen threat; الغيب may modify the person or the fear.
rows.anchor: وبالغيب حال من المفعول، أي وهو غائب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of fear with the name al-Raḥmān highlights the worshipper's awareness of God's vast mercy even while fearing Him.
rows.anchor: وقرن بالخشية الرحمن بناء على الخاشي، حيث علم أنه واسع الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering in peace means either safety from punishment or receiving God's and the angels' greeting.
rows.anchor: ادخلوها بسلام: أي سالمين من العذاب، أو مسلما عليكم من الله وملائكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day of abiding parallels the disbelievers' day of warning and means entering while destined to remain forever.
rows.anchor: ذلك يوم الخلود: كقوله: فادخلوها خالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise receive everything their wishes encompass, plus an unspecified increase beyond it; he links this to hidden delights and a prophetic report.
rows.anchor: لهم ما يشاؤن فيها: أي ما تعلقت به مشيئاتهم من أنواع الملاذ والكرامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proposed meanings of the extra gift include multiplying a good deed tenfold, spouses from Paradise, or God's self-disclosure so that the blessed see Him.
rows.anchor: فقيل: مضاعفة الحسنة بعشر أمثالها. وقيل: أزواج من حور الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroyed generations before the Quraysh had greater might and wealth; their travels through lands yielded no escape from destruction.
rows.anchor: أهلكنا: أي قبل قريش. هم أشد منهم بطشا، لكثرة قوتهم وأموالهم

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses نقبت for roaming far and wide, though another transmission has طوفت; al-Ḥārith ibn Khilda also uses it for traversing the lands.
rows.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس في معنى التطواف: وقد نقبت في الآفاق حتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in فنقبوا may refer to earlier mighty peoples who traveled through the lands, or to the Quraysh exploring the lands of those destroyed and finding no refuge.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يعود الضمير في فنقبوا على قريش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن يعمر وأبو العالية ونصر بن يسار وأبو حيوة والأصمعي
rows.claim: These readers address the people of Mecca with an imperative: travel through the lands and investigate what became of earlier nations.
rows.anchor: بكسر القاف مشددة على الأمر لأهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A light-kasra reading may mean that their feet or camels' hooves became worn from traveling so much.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: بكسر القاف خفيفة، أي نقبت أقدامهم وأخفاف إبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هل من محيص may report them asking whether any escape remains, or rhetorically establish that there is no escape from death.
rows.anchor: واحتمل أن لا يكون ثم قول، أي لا محيص من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person with a heart has an alert intellect; the heart stands for understanding, and one who has no understanding is as if heartless.
rows.anchor: لمن كان له قلب: أي واع، والمعنى: لمن له عقل وعبر عنه بمحله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers make the person actively listen, with السمع as its object; شهيد means present and attentive, while Qatāda's reading can mean someone versed in scripture who recognizes the truth.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أو ألقى السمع، مبنيا للفاعل، والسمع نصب به

rows.speaker: السلمي وطلحة والسدي وأبو البرهسم
rows.claim: These readers use the passive ألقي, making the hearing something cast upon the attentive person; Abū Ḥayyān also considers someone opening another person's ear while both remain alert.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي، وطلحة، والسدي، وأبو البرهسم: أو ألقي مبنيا، للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's closing command to remind with the Quran echoes its opening oath by Qāf and the Quran.
rows.anchor: وختمت بقوله: فذكر بالقرآن، كما افتتحت ب ق والقرآن

none: Quran verse text only; the segment contains no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the people of the right, the surah turns to the people of the left; the question intensifies the magnitude of their calamity.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر حال السابقين، وأتبعهم بأصحاب الميمنة، ذكر حال أصحاب المشئمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو مالك وابن زيد والجمهور
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Abū Mālik, Ibn Zayd, and most exegetes identify اليحموم as smoke; Ibn ʿAbbās also calls it a canopy of fire enclosing the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو مالك وابن زيد والجمهور: دخان

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysān says اليحموم is one of the names of Hell; Ibn Zayd and Ibn Burayda say it is a black mountain in Hell where its people seek refuge but find greater torment.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: اليحموم من أسماء جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shade is named as shade but lacks its ordinary coolness and benefit; 'not noble' either completes its blame or describes the humiliation of those sheltering there.
rows.anchor: لا بارد ولا كريم: صفتان للظل نفيتا

rows.speaker: ابن عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbla reads the two adjectives in the nominative, meaning that the shade itself is neither cool nor noble.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: لا بارد ولا كريم بجرهما وابن عبلة: برفعهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' worldly luxury is condemned because indulgence leads to idleness and neglect of reflection on the hereafter.
rows.anchor: فيه ذم الترف والتنعم في الدنيا، والترف طريق إلى البطالة

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Ibn Zayd identify the great sin to which they persisted as associating partners with God; Abū Ḥayyān prefers this because the next clause is distinct.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والضحاك وابن زيد: الشرك، وهو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the alternative that the great sin is denial of resurrection, since 'they used to say' is conjoined with the preceding clause and signals a different offense.
rows.anchor: ويبعده: وكانوا يقولون، فإنه معطوف على ما قبله، والعطف يقتضي التغاير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the conjunction before 'or our forefathers' as coordinated with the pronoun in 'will we be raised,' licensed by the intervening interrogative hamza; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this parsing.
rows.anchor: كيف حسن العطف على المضمر في لمبعوثون من غير تأكيد بنحن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the grammarians, he says the conjunction itself coordinates the phrase with what precedes; the interrogative hamza is understood after the conjunction because questions must begin with it.
rows.anchor: بل الواو والفاء لعطف ما بعدهما على ما قبلهما، والهمزة في التقدير متأخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is commanded to announce the resurrection of all generations for judgment and the punishment awaiting deniers; the appointed time is the world's fixed endpoint.
rows.anchor: أمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يخبرهم ببعث العالم، أولهم وآخرهم، للحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address targets Quraysh and everyone like them; من in 'from a tree of zaqqūm' may mark origin, partitive meaning, or species, depending on its syntax.
rows.anchor: ثم إنكم: خطاب لكفار قريش، أيها الضالون عن الهدى

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads شجرة in the feminine singular instead of the collective شجر.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: من شجر وعبد الله: من شجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'drink from it' can refer to the eaten food or the act of eating; al-Zamakhsharī instead connects masculine عليه with the masculine noun شجر.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والضمير في عليه عائد على المأكول، أو على الأكل

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamza read شُرْب with ḍamma, while Mujāhid and Abū ʿUthmān read the kasra form as a name for the drink; most readers use the regular verbal noun with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وحمزة: شرب بضم الشين، وهو مصدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take الهيم as camels afflicted by thirst; other views derive it from a female camel, wandering men and women, or thirsty sands.
rows.anchor: والهيم، قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك: جمع أهيم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says starvation drives them to eat zaqqūm and then thirst forces them to drink boiling water as thirst-stricken camels drink.
rows.anchor: أنه يسلط عليهم من الجوع ما يضطرهم إلى أكل الزقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two drinking clauses describe successive horrors: hot water worsens thirst, then they drink another futile draught like thirsty camels; the verbs are not redundant, contrary to the objection al-Zamakhsharī answers.
rows.anchor: والفاء تقتضي التعقيب في الشربين، وأنهم أولا لما عطشوا شربوا من الحميم

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن وخارجة عن نافع ونعيم ومحبوب وأبو زيد وهارون وعصمة وعباس
rows.claim: These transmitters read نُزُل with a silent zāy, meaning the first food offered to a guest; Abū Ḥayyān says the word mocks the disbelievers and cites a poem about spears and swords as a host's welcome.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن وخارجة، عن نافع ونعيم ومحبوب وأبو زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to believe urges acceptance of resurrection just as the people acknowledge their first creation; he also reads it as a reproach backed by the following proofs.
rows.anchor: فلولا تصدقون بالإعادة وتقرون بها، كما أقررتم بالنشأة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seed fluid is something humans emit without control or capacity to create it, so its origin points to God's creative power.
rows.anchor: وهو المني الذي يخرج من الإنسان، إذ ليس له في خلقه عمل ولا إرادة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī interprets خلق as forming and measuring the semen's shape rather than bringing it into existence.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: يخلقونه: تقدرونه وتصورونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza clause can be analyzed as a subject and predicate, but more naturally the separated pronoun is the subject of an omitted verb such as 'Do you create it?'; أم is probably disjunctive and begins a second question.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن يكون فاعلا بفعل محذوف، كأنه قال: أتخلقونه؟

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads قدرنا with a light dāl, meaning that God decreed and fixed death or arranged its occurrence in sequence rather than all at once.
rows.anchor: والجمهور: قدرنا، بشد الدال وابن كثير: يخفها، أي قضينا وأثبتنا

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī connects 'to replace your likes' to decreeing death: one generation dies and another replaces it; Abū Ḥayyān notes that another parse links it to God's inability to be overcome.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: المعنى نحن قادرون، قدرنا بينكم الموت، على أن نبدل أمثالكم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the unknown transformation as changing people into apes and pigs, fitting the passage's threatening tone.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: من كونكم قردة وخنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمثالكم may mean replacements or your current attributes: God can destroy and recreate people, or alter their physical and moral qualities into forms beyond their knowledge.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أمثالكم جمع مثل بمعنى الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first creation may refer to each person's known origin or to Adam's creation from clay; reflection on it should lead to belief in a later creation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نشأة آدم، وأنه خلق من طين، ولا ينكرها أحد من ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the passage urges analogical reasoning, Abū Ḥayyān says it supports only the a fortiori form of analogy, not every type of qiyās.
rows.anchor: ولا تدل إلا على قياس الأولى، لا على جميع أنواع القياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People till and sow, but God alone makes the crop grow to maturity for their benefit; حطاما is dry, crumbled vegetation without useful grain.
rows.anchor: أفرأيتم ما تحرثون: ما تذرونه في الأرض وتبذرونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes that تفكه belongs to the same verb family as تخرج and تحوب.
rows.anchor: وتفكه من أخوات تخرج وتحوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains تفكهون as casting aside one's delight: a person يفكه is carefree and buoyant, so the verse depicts their delight turning to distress.
rows.anchor: تطرحون الفكاهة عن أنفسكم وهي المسرة

rows.speaker: عبد الله والجحدري
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh and al-Jaḥdarī read the verb with doubled lām, while the public reading has a single lām; readers also vary the vowel of ẓāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله والجحدري: فظللتم على الأصل، بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: أبو حرام
rows.claim: Abū Ḥarām reads تفكنون with nūn instead of hāʾ; Ibn Khālawayh distinguishes its sense as regret from تفكه, wonder.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تفكهون وأبو حرام: بالنون بدل الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause 'we are surely ruined' has an omitted speech verb introducing what the disbelievers say; مغرمون may mean punished with severe torment or burdened by the cost of the crop.
rows.anchor: إنا لمغرمون، قبله محذوف: أي يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They then say they have been deprived of any share in good; the description of drinkable water already conveys its contrast with bitter water.
rows.anchor: بل نحن محرومون: محدودون، لا حظ لنا في الخير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains why the conditional particle appears before the crop's destruction but not before the water's becoming bitter, and adds that food is more basic than drink; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the weak grammarians' claim that the later outcome depends on the earlier outcome being impossible.
rows.anchor: والذي ذكره سيبويه: إنها حرف لما كان سيقع لوقوع الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree is the wood from which fire is struck; construing the tree itself as fire is an unnecessarily strained metaphor.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن شجرتها، المراد منه الشجر الذي يقدح منه النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire serves as a reminder of Hell and a provision for people camped in barren land or travelers; Ibn Zayd's gloss 'the hungry' is very weak.
rows.anchor: ومتاعا للمقوين: أي النازلين الأرض القوا، وهي القفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage presents four signs related to human creation and life's food, drink, and fire; fire especially points to resurrection through transformation, and God's unique creation warrants glorification.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأربعة التي ذكرها الله تعالى ووقفهم عليها، من أمر خلقهم وما به قوام عيشهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation treats لا as an emphatic extra particle, making the phrase a direct oath; another understands a denial of the disbelievers' claim before beginning the oath, but Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because it requires deleting both parts of لا's clause without a question prompting it.
rows.anchor: فقيل: لا زائدة مؤكدة مثلها في قوله: لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وبعض النحاة
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and some grammarians say the denied proposition is omitted before a fresh oath, but Abū Ḥayyān rules out this deletion without a prior question.
rows.anchor: قاله سعيد بن جبير وبعض النحاة ولا يجوز، لأن في ذلك حذف اسم لا وخبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further account takes لا as a rhetorical opening that intensifies the oath, as in established speech patterns.
rows.anchor: وقيل: توكيد مبالغة ما، وهي كاستفتاح كلام شبهه في القسم
